chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: Why he left Cab: wanting to teach; Don Redman
summary: With a baby coming, Thomas leaves the road, remembering Don Redman as a giant writer who loved quarts of ice cream.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Why did you leave Cab's band?

I left... See, I made up my band... My wife was pregnant. And I had just had the road, and I had this aspiration to teach. So I took it all the way out there. Teachers stay in town. So I told you the story. I went to him and said, "Fess, I've got to give my notice." He said, "You can't do that." I already had my gig. I already had my job with Don Redman.

So I went with Don, and I had a great experience with Don. That was great to work with him, because he was another giant. He could write, boy. Don Redman didn't care nothin' about the key of D and the key of E. It was just as easy to him as the key of C. And he wrote. And he could play, too. See, he played lead on all his arrangements. And he was a beautiful guy. I got close to him. I used to hang out with him when the gig was over. I'd go uptown with him...
I've got some pictures of you and Tyree and him together.

And he loved ice cream. The last thing he'd have at night would be a quart of ice cream. And you know he wouldn't ever give you none of it! He'd take you up to his apartment and everything, he'd very politely ask you if you wanted it, but he gave you so little you'd wish you

hadn't asked him. But that was his thing. Like, if we was going to go and get a drink or something, he went and got him a quart of ice cream -- and he'd eat all of it. He was such a nice guy to get along with. And I had the privilege of playing...
He was a short and (?) man.
Yeah. He could play that horn. And could write.
